evidence: The entry claimed 175s of serial-only time inside a 170s total; the agent conceded the figures came from two incomparable runs (a contended baseline -json sum vs a quiet wall clock) and restated from one run (174s wall, 170s serial sum).
guidance_note: Before writing any arithmetic claim into a changelog, take every figure in the sentence from one measurement run and check that the parts fit inside the whole.

evidence: The hunk places engineConstructMu.Lock() after the `return nil, loadErr` check, so the I/O-bound load and journal-lock phases the reviewer names as slow run outside the lock; the reviewer's 'stuck past its deadline behind a slow construction' scenario rests on work the lock does not enclose. That NewSqlEngine itself is only milliseconds is the agent's claim and is not measurable from the packet.
The reviewer listed about 24 other internal packages with tests against the entry's 'eleven'; the agent agreed and corrected it to 'two dozen'.
guidance_note: Recount any specific number in a changelog against the repo (e.g. `go list ./...`) instead of carrying a figure from earlier notes.

evidence: TestInitAdoptHardStopsOnTimeout calls t.Parallel() while assigning the package vars adoptRemoteTicketsBlockingFn/adoptRemoteTimeout, which the PR's own convention keeps serial; the agent conceded that its sweep missed bare package-var assignments, then re-swept.
guidance_note: When building a serial-exclusion set, sweep for every assignment to a package-level var from test code (direct and via helpers), not just t.Setenv and known hooks — the agent ran exactly this stronger sweep only after the finding.

evidence: The diff bumped the patch count to five and added a Patch 5 section, but the refresh checklist still said 'all three' and walked only patches 1-4; the agent agreed and added a Patch 5 step.
guidance_note: When adding an entry to an enumerated list in a doc, grep the same doc for every other place that counts or walks that list and update them together.

evidence: 367+21≠387 was real, but the reviewer's proposed correction (367→366) was wrong: the agent's exact grep found 388 test funcs, so the stale figure was the total, and the entry became 388/367/21.
guidance_note: Derive every count in a sentence from one grep run on the branch rather than mixing a fresh count with an inherited one.

narrative: One review round raised six findings: four changelog accuracy defects (impossible timing arithmetic, a wrong package count, a wrong test total, a stale patch checklist), one real parallel-test global-mutation miss, and one ctx-aware-mutex suggestion. The agent fixed the five real ones in one commit, rejected the reviewer's wrong count correction in favour of the right one, and pushed back with sound reasoning on the mutex. The second round was clean.
guidance_observations: Four of the six findings were numbers in prose the agent wrote from memory or from mixed measurements; one verification pass over the changelog's figures before opening the PR would have removed most of the round.
The agent checked the reviewer's proposed numeric correction independently instead of applying it, which avoided shipping a second wrong number.

evidence: OpenSync ran CALL DOLT_BRANCH('-m', ...) on s.db outside the commit lock while Open wrapped the same call in withCommitLock, so the race was real. The agent applied the reviewer's literal cure (an unconditional withCommitLock around the whole check), and that cure made every read-only OpenSync queue behind snapshot holds, which became F15.
guidance_note: Before wrapping a mostly-read operation in a lock, ask which callers take that path and how long the lock can be held; lock only the mutation (double-checked) so read-only opens never wait on a no-op.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 (an unlocked rename racing OpenForRead's migrate under the commit lock). The agent applied the same unconditional withCommitLock, which produced the F15 liveness regression.
guidance_note: When two reviewers prescribe the same cure, still trace the cure's effect on every caller of the function before applying it.

evidence: openFreshWorkspace was switched to migratedDoltDir, so TestConvergedSchemaDumpIsDeterministic compared two copies of a single migration run; the 715fc41 diff reverts it to filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "dolt") with a comment saying why.
guidance_note: When moving tests onto a shared fixture, read each test's doc comment for its premise and exempt any test whose subject is the work the fixture skips (here, migration determinism).

evidence: The original WalkDir returned early on d.IsDir(), leaving directories writable, and rename(2) is gated by the directory's write bit. 715fc41 adds freezeTemplate stamping dirs 0o555 and thaws them in TestMain.
guidance_note: When a mechanism promises 'fails loudly at first write', enumerate the write syscalls it must block (open-for-write, rename, unlink, create) and check each one is gated.

evidence: The test's pristine stage exists to reach LocalIssueCount's tableExists==0 short-circuit, which a pre-migrated template copy cannot reach; 715fc41 restores the from-scratch root with a comment.
guidance_note: Same move as F3: before swapping a fixture, check whether any test stage depends on the state the fixture skips past.

evidence: Every OpenSync in the suite ran on an already-master store, so the new rename path was never exercised; 715fc41 adds TestOpenSyncNormalizesPreMadeMainBranchToMaster using a shared premadeMainBranchDB helper.
guidance_note: When moving a duty to a new call site, add a test that drives each new site down its mutating branch, not only the site the old test happened to cover.

evidence: rootB moved to unrelatedDoltDir with its own t.TempDir parent, so the comment saying rootB and rootC share lock paths became false; 715fc41 rewrites it.
guidance_note: When changing how a test variable is constructed, re-read the comments in that test that explain behaviour in terms of the old construction.

evidence: The CHANGELOG still said 'under the commit lock in Open, on the mirror's connection in OpenSync' after 715fc41 wrapped OpenSync's rename in withCommitLock; the fix commit touched sync.go but not the changelog sentence describing it.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a mechanism the PR's changelog describes, grep the changelog and PR body for that mechanism in the same commit.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: the round-0 hunk already shows buildStoreTemplate returning `"", nil, err` after MkdirTemp on every error path, so the leak predates 715fc41, which only swapped in freezeTemplate. The fix in 5b42264 adds a success-gated defer that thaws and removes base.
guidance_note: When creating a resource outside every automatic cleanup scope (MkdirTemp outside t.TempDir), add the success-gated defer in the same edit.

evidence: Duplicate of F8: the changelog's 'on the mirror's connection in OpenSync' asymmetry was left stale by 715fc41's commit-lock wrap.
guidance_note: Same as F8: sweep prose describing a mechanism in the commit that changes the mechanism.

evidence: Duplicate of F9. The flag is a false positive: the empty-dir-on-error leak was in the original buildStoreTemplate (round-0 hunk), not introduced by 715fc41.
Third duplicate of the stale 'on the mirror's connection in OpenSync' changelog parenthetical left by 715fc41.

The flag is a false positive: 5b42264 touched only CHANGELOG.md and fixture_test.go, and the bare-path→migratedDoltDir swap in workspace_lock_test.go was part of the original PR's bulk conversion. The flock tests only derive sibling paths, so the template is pure cost; 95d1b51 reverts them.
guidance_note: Convert a test to a store fixture only when the test reads the store; a bulk find-and-replace of `filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "dolt")` catches path-only tests too.

evidence: Permission bits are inert under CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE, so the freeze guarantee is not universal, but the reviewer itself could not show CI runs as root. The agent took the reviewer's 'document the caveat' option in 95d1b51. The flag is a false positive: the chmod-based freeze predates 5b42264.

The 715fc41 diff makes OpenSync call s.withCommitLock unconditionally, so read-only callers (sync status, mirror cycles) that never touched the commit lock before now wait behind snapshot holds of up to about 15 minutes. 95d1b51 splits out the lock-free masterRenameSource and locks only when a rename is due, with a liveness test.
guidance_note: When adding a lock acquisition to an open path, list that path's read-only callers and the lock's longest holder before committing.

evidence: The 'creation, migration, adoption, or recovery keep building from nothing' sentence was in the original changelog (5b42264's diff leaves it untouched), while promote/rawdump/adopt tests were moved onto the template. The flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When writing a rule in prose about which tests use a fixture, derive it by grepping the fixture's call sites and the from-scratch sites, not from intent.

evidence: The 'verified by mutation (share the template: the freeze refuses the open)' text predates 95d1b51 and says mutation, not test, so 'implies a CI test' overstates it; still, no committed test pinned the freeze. The agent took the stronger option and added TestFrozenTemplateRefusesDirectOpen in 612170c. The flag is a false positive: the sentence is original.
guidance_note: When a guarantee was proven by a manual mutation run, commit that mutation as a test in the same PR rather than citing it in prose.

evidence: 95d1b51 rewrote the changelog's from-scratch rule for F16 into an enumerated categorization but left out TestLocalIssueCountAcrossLifecycle, which the F5 fix had made from-scratch for a different reason.
guidance_note: When rewriting an enumerated claim, regenerate the list from a grep of every from-scratch site (`filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "dolt")`) and check each one is covered.

evidence: 95d1b51 added the no-queueing liveness claim and TestOpenSyncOnNormalizedStoreIgnoresHeldCommitLock, but the same sentence still said 'the test that pinned the old site now pins both halves' and named only the EnsureDatabase test.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a test and a changelog claim together, update the changelog's list of backing tests in the same edit.

evidence: The test name says EnsureDatabase renames, while the body (rewritten in the original PR, per the round-0 changelog's 'pins both halves') asserts it leaves the branch untouched. 612170c added only the frozen-template test and changelog text, so the flag is a false positive.
guidance_note: When inverting what a test asserts, rename the test in the same edit so the name states the new contract.

evidence: The F18 fix in 612170c added one more category to the 'exhaustive' from-scratch list without sweeping for others; the three schema-skew tests still built from scratch with no stated reason. They arguably fall under the migration-chain category, as the agent said, so the defect is a missing explanation rather than a wrong rule.
guidance_note: When a reviewer finds one missing item in an enumerated list, re-derive the whole list from the code instead of appending the one item.

evidence: The 388/367 counts belong to the earlier PR #417 entry and are the denominators of its 474s→141s measurement, so updating them to ~392/371 would corrupt that claim; anchoring them in time fixes the present-tense ambiguity. Not fix-caused in the audit's sense: the ambiguity of a historical entry predates this PR.
guidance_note: Phrase counts in changelog entries as measurements at that change ('as measured when this landed') so later test additions don't read as drift.

narrative: Five review rounds hit the cap. Seven of 22 findings were caused by earlier fixes: the verbatim unconditional commit-lock fix for F1/F2 left three duplicate changelog drift findings, caused a real liveness regression (F15), and that fix in turn left a stale test list in the changelog (F19). The changelog's from-scratch categorization was patched one item at a time (F16→F18→F21) instead of being re-derived. Every round also surfaced pre-existing defects the reviewer had missed earlier (leaky template build, path-only tests on the fixture, stale test name), so no round was purely fix-caused and avoidable_rounds is a floor of 0.
guidance_observations: Applying the reviewer's literal cure (an unconditional lock) without tracing its callers bought a regression round; the double-checked shape the agent ended with was available at round 0.

The long hand-written changelog paragraph was the main source of findings: each code fix left a sentence describing the old mechanism, and each enumerated claim was patched rather than regenerated from the code.
Round-0 bulk conversion of tests to the template fixture produced three later findings (F3, F5, F13) of the same kind: a test whose premise or needs didn't fit the fixture.

evidence: The reviewer's per-test counts (wedge tests ~3 lit invocations, eager test ~4) contradict 'every one of these tests drives dozens'; the agent agreed and narrowed the claim in the changelog, PR body and ticket.
guidance_note: Before writing 'every one of these' in prose, check the claim against each named item, not just the largest one.

evidence: The eager-push test enables auto-sync and spawns the same detached mirror as its siblings but lacked their awaitMirrorQuiescence guard against the t.TempDir RemoveAll race; the agent added it at the siblings' placement.
guidance_note: When opting a group of tests into t.Parallel(), diff each one's cleanup guards against its siblings that spawn the same background processes.

evidence: Contention can in principle stretch exit latency, but the 4s bound must stay under interrupt.DefaultGrace (5s) to tell a clean exit from a grace-timer kill, so widening it removes the assertion. The agent also noted cross-package concurrency already loaded these tests. The decisive argument is the grace discriminator, not the cited law.

narrative: One round raised three findings: an overstated changelog claim, a missing mirror-quiescence guard on a newly parallel test, and a request to widen SIGTERM deadlines. The agent fixed the first two and correctly refused to widen a deadline whose position below the 5s grace timer is the assertion itself. Round 1 approved with nothing new.
guidance_observations: The quiescence miss is the per-test version of the sibling-consistency check: when parallelizing, compare each test's guards against siblings with the same subprocess shape.

evidence: nightly.yml, the Justfile and CONTRIBUTING.md still carry -timeout 30m, so 'the repository's only committed -timeout 30m override' was false; the agent scoped the claim to the graph-audit workflow.
guidance_note: Before writing 'the only X in the repository', run the grep that proves it and keep the claim to what the grep shows.

evidence: Duplicate of F1 on the same line; it also notes nightly.yml's own justification comment. Fixed by the same edit in b6a659d.
600s/130s ≈ 4.6x, not 6x, and the workflow comment quoted only one 100s sample. The agent restated both measured runs (100s, 129s) and claimed better than 4x.
guidance_note: When quoting a range and a derived ratio together, compute the ratio at the range's worst end.

evidence: One sample was thin evidence, which is the real part of the finding. With two samples (100s, 129s) the default 10m alarm keeps more than 4.6x headroom on a weekly, retryable report job, and re-adding a buffer recreates the hidden slowness the epic removed. The law token is a stretch: no error is swallowed either way.
guidance_note: When removing a timeout on the strength of measurements, cite every available sample in the code comment from the start, not a single day.

evidence: TestClassify and TestLinkedModulesDeterministic are parallel and never read nativeLibs, so 'every parallel test in the package reads it' was false; the comment was narrowed.

narrative: One round raised five findings, four of them prose overclaims (a repo-wide 'only' claim twice, a ratio computed at the best end of a range, an 'every' in a comment) and one request to re-add a timeout buffer. The agent fixed the overclaims and argued the timeout pushback with added data, which the round-1 reviewer accepted. No fix caused a later finding.
guidance_observations: Every accepted finding was an absolute word ('only', 'every') or a best-case ratio in prose; a self-check of quantifiers against a grep before pushing would have cleared the round.

evidence: The agent tested a mid-test os.Exit and reports that the go tool still emits a package-level fail with Elapsed, refuting the 'package vanishes' half; the stranded buffered output half was real and was fixed with an end-of-stream flush and a test. The packet carries only the agent's report of the experiment, not its output.
guidance_note: When writing a stream consumer that buffers per-key, decide at design time what happens to buffers still open at EOF.

evidence: packageResult.Failed was set in consume and read nowhere; the agent took the reviewer's 'wire it up' option and marked failed rows as not calibration points, with a test.
guidance_note: Every field added to a result struct needs a reader in the same PR; grep for reads before committing.

evidence: The budgets[path]-else-default lookup appears verbatim in both enforce and printTable (both visible in the hunk); budgetFor was extracted.
guidance_note: When a second function needs a lookup rule the first already implements, extract it rather than copying it.

evidence: printTable, which the PR says produces the calibration record, had no test; the agent added one pinning order, budget column and the failure mark.
guidance_note: Every function a doc names as producing a durable artifact gets a test in the PR that introduces it.

evidence: The tools/licenses entry was 60s, identical to defaultBudget, against the file's own 'graduate to an explicit entry' policy. The agent took the reviewer's second option, a distinct justified number (40s vs a 30s default) after re-baselining.
guidance_note: When writing an explicit table entry beside a default, check that it differs from the default and that its comment says why.

evidence: The reviewer hedged ('moderate confidence'). The agent reports observing go test -json emit a package-level {"Action":"fail",...,"FailedBuild":...} after build-output/build-fail, which the existing terminal case already captures. That matches current test2json behaviour, where build-fail is keyed by ImportPath and a package fail follows.

GitHub Actions documents an unspecified shell on Linux as `bash -e {0}`, and only an explicit `shell: bash` gives `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}`, so the reviewer had the default backwards and the line does enable pipefail.

narrative: One round raised seven findings on a new CI budget tool. The agent fixed four real ones (an unread Failed field, a duplicated budget lookup, an untested printTable, a budget entry equal to the default), split one finding by testing it (refuted the vanishing package, fixed the stranded output), and correctly rejected two wrong premises about test2json build-fail and the GitHub Actions default shell. No fix caused a later finding.
guidance_observations: The agent checked the reviewer's two hedged schema claims by running them before deciding, which is why both pushbacks were right.
The accepted findings were standard completeness checks on new code (every field read, every rendered artifact tested, one home per rule) that a self-review before opening the PR would catch.
